_comment: Maps every run: step in .github/workflows/ci.yml to the scripts/handoff-loop.sh gate that covers it locally. Read by .github/scripts/gate_parity_lint.py. An unmapped step FAILS — silence is not an exemption. Three categories: a gate name (covered), 'environment' (sets the stage, detects no defect in your code), or 'not-runnable-locally' WITH a reason (a real hole in local coverage, kept short on purpose).
_scope: ci.yml only. The other PR-triggered workflows — design-lint, fail-open-check, pgtap-pilot, smoke_surface_gate, the drift checks — are path-filtered specialists that mostly need services a laptop lacks. They are NOT covered here, so a green handoff-loop.sh still does not predict their red. Named so it stays visible.

ci.yml::Install ruff.reason: installs the linter; the venv already has it

ci.yml::Baseline ratchet (enforcement ma.note: CI runs this PR-only with BASELINE_BASE_SHA from the event; the local gate resolves the same value from the merge-base with origin/main.

ci.yml::Install dependencies.reason: pip install / npm ci; the local checkout is already installed

ci.yml::Start Pi CEO server locally.reason: starts the server the smoke test then exercises

ci.yml::Show server log on failure.reason: diagnostic output on an already-failed run

ci.yml::Run smoke test against productio.reason: probes the live Railway deployment. Runs after merge, so no local gate can predict it — and by design nothing on a laptop should be able to.
